claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest and exegete, active during the first half of the fifth century.
Hesychius served as a presbyter (priest) in the church in Jerusalem around 412.
Hesychius was renowned in the Eastern Church as a theologian, biblical commentator, and preacher.
By 429, Hesychius was recognized as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
Hesychius died around 450, though this date is uncertain.
The work In Lazarum et in ramos palmarum is a homily on Lazarus and the Palm Branches, attributed to Hesychius as 'Hesychiou, presbyterou Hierosolymon' (Hesychius, priest of Jerusalem).
The homily was formerly transmitted under the name of Titus of Bostra.
Hesychius' homilies on the resurrection of Lazarus are connected to the liturgical celebration in Jerusalem, where residents gathered in Bethany to read the account of Jesus' raising of Lazarus.
The work survives in manuscript form, including in the Patriarchal Library of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem (manuscript 136, folios 109-112).
Hesychius played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ and was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
Hesychius was a prolific preacher and exegete whose works are important for understanding early Christian biblical interpretation and liturgical preaching in Jerusalem.
